objective: Review current Foundry-Go for vulnerabilities and important missing features.

scope.method: Inventory all current families against the unchanged previous acceptance snapshot; fresh risk-focused source tracing, public-API probes, dependency scans and selected existing tests. Not an every-line review or deployment penetration test.

source_inventory.excludes: Hidden directories, bin, node_modules, vendor; only .go/.ts/.mjs/.lua. Build/dependency inputs separately fingerprinted.

previous_source_comparison.outside_inventory_disposition: Three existing release-tool source files were not included in the previous runtime/generator/client snapshot; they are fingerprinted by this audit.

findings.title: Cookie authentication without BrowserSessions does not prevent caching of personalized responses
findings.evidence: Raw and typed JSON handlers both return distinct account-specific 200 responses with no Cache-Control/Pragma and Vary only Sec-Fetch-Site and Origin. The raw handler also sets Last-Modified.
findings.condition: Disclosure requires an intermediary that caches these cookie requests/responses; no production proxy exploit was performed. BrowserSessions already sets no-store.
findings.recommendation: Apply the cookie-response cache policy in the shared authentication owner, covering required/optional paths and early failures; add regressions for both cookie entry points.

gaps.title: Repository-owned CI/security checks and reporting policy
gaps.absence: No checked-in .github/.circleci/.buildkite workflows, .gitlab-ci.yml, Jenkinsfile, azure-pipelines.yml or SECURITY.md found. External CI and hosting settings were not inspected.
gaps.acceptance: Reuse native verification and required-backend/tool modes in automation; run scanner independently of cold package measurement, interpret actual findings, and document supported versions/private disclosure channel using confirmed maintainer details.

gaps.title: Opt-in typed outbound destination policy
gaps.acceptance: Validate permitted schemes/ports/hosts and actual resolved IPv4/IPv6 addresses at connection time, handle DNS changes and proxies explicitly, and test loopback/private/link-local rejection plus approved internal endpoints. Preserve ordinary internal-service clients.
gaps.classification: Capability gap; generic loopback connectivity is intended and is not alone a framework SSRF vulnerability.

gaps.title: Reusable inbound webhook verification
gaps.acceptance: Bound and preserve original signed bytes, verify provider signatures with rotated secrets and timestamp tolerance, expose verified delivery/account identity, then reuse existing idempotency/outbox. Test tampering, expiry, duplicate valid delivery and tenant scoping.

gaps.priority: before low-downtime migrations on large live tables
gaps.title: Explicit nontransactional PostgreSQL migrations
gaps.acceptance: Add an explicit execution mode while retaining runner locking, failed/uncertain progress and reconciliation. Support CONCURRENTLY without pretending SQL and history are atomic; test interruption/recovery without automatic destructive cleanup.

already_present: Generics and tagged unions in shared schema/client contracts
Inbound idempotency with current authorization on replay

environment.services: existing local PostgreSQL and Redis; no new services or destructive reset

batches.service: existing loopback service observed listening; no service started
batches.name: redis-tests

verification.failure_disposition: Initial persistence batch failed only Redis due to missing FOUNDRY_TEST_REDIS_ADDR; observed the existing listener, selected it, and reran ./redis/... successfully. Redis/data and redis/raw were cached on correction. Package skips are packages with no tests; only actual test skips were unconfigured real AWS/R2 certification.

scanner_disposition.framework_and_consumer: Only module-level GO-2026-5932 for x/crypto; no affected package or function trace. The affected OpenPGP package is not used by the reviewed source.
scanner_disposition.gopls: Three module-level advisories; no affected symbols reported for scanned binary. Reassess when upgrading development tooling.
scanner_disposition.qualification: Dependency scans cover the reported database snapshot and reachable analysis, not unknown flaws, all reflection/plugin behavior or deployed configuration.

documentation_check.output: Documentation links, blueprint numbering, and fixture Go requirements are valid.

limitations: No new full make verify, race, fuzz, gopls completion or TypeScript runtime run: unchanged runtime/generator/client hashes match the separate full acceptance baseline; this audit ran selected security/persistence tests and fresh scans.
Live AWS and R2 certification tests skipped because provider configuration is absent.
No production proxy, deployment secrets, external CI or hosted security-reporting settings were inspected.
No runtime fix or gap implementation performed; S01 and G01-G04 remain recommendations.
